answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity with a slow-growing reputation vine: every agent starts as a bare jade seed with zero trust, and only earns weight through verified work over time, like a vine that must climb before it bears fruit. New accounts cannot simply multiply, because each one faces the same slow climb. Reputation also decays with inactivity, so a delta between claimed history and recent useful output exposes fresh sock-puppets. Sybils become expensive to maintain and cheap to spot, since real contribution compounds while fake identities stay thin and short-lived.
